contents: # Patrols module (uhifadhi/patrol-module). dev_tools registers the
# patrol:seed:* commands — dev/test only, so production never grows commands
# that fabricate patrols.
# The deployment's observation vocabulary — the design's six capture chips
# (uhifadhi-mobile flow.html), which the Doria app sends verbatim. Keys are
# the stored wire values; labels are what the web UI shows.
patrol:
observation_categories:
wildlife:   { label: Wildlife }
carcass:    { label: Carcass }
snare_trap: { label: 'Snare / trap' }
hwc_sign:   { label: 'HWC sign' }
livestock:  { label: Livestock }
human_sign: { label: 'Human sign' }
when@dev:
patrol:
dev_tools: true
when@test:
patrol:
dev_tools: true
# THE ONE LINE THIS RECIPE CANNOT WRITE — and it is REQUIRED, not an extra you
# add later.
# Five columns on this module's tables name a PERSON: who led the patrol, who
# put it on hold, who recorded the observation, who acted on the event, who
# signed the amendment. The accounts of an installation are not this module's,
# so all five are mapped to an interface that uhifadhi/module-contracts
# publishes, and you resolve that interface to your own class. A recipe has no
# way to know what you call your people.
# HOW FAR YOU GET WITHOUT IT — honestly. The bundle installs, the container
# compiles, and the kernel boots. What you CANNOT do is touch the schema.
# Anything that walks the metadata — `doctrine:schema:create`,
# `doctrine:schema:update`, `doctrine:migrations:diff` — stops on the
# unresolved interface:
#   In MappingException.php line 72:
#     Class 'Uhifadhi\ModuleContracts\Entity\UserInterface' does not exist
# IF YOU INSTALLED uhifadhi/team-module THERE IS NOTHING TO DO. Team provides
# the account class, so team states the resolution from its own bundle (0.3.2
# and later) and this step is already answered:
#   doctrine:
#       orm:
#           resolve_target_entities:
#               Uhifadhi\ModuleContracts\Entity\UserInterface: Uhifadhi\Team\Entity\User
# You do not write that. It is here so you can recognise it in `debug:config
# doctrine` and know where it came from.
# OTHERWISE — no team, or an account class of your own — IT IS YOURS, and it is
# one line naming your class instead. It has to answer the contract's seven
# questions — getId, getUuidString, getEmail, getFirstName, getLastName,
# getFullName, getRangerCode — and be in the mapping chain:
#   doctrine:
#       orm:
#           resolve_target_entities:
#               Uhifadhi\ModuleContracts\Entity\UserInterface: App\Entity\Person
# YOUR ANSWER WINS EVEN WITH TEAM INSTALLED. Team's is prepended, and prepended
# configuration loses to the application's — so naming your own class is all it
# takes, and there is nothing to disable first.
# MERGE IT INTO THE BLOCK ALREADY THERE. config/packages/doctrine.yaml opens
# with `doctrine:`, and a second `doctrine:` key in the same file is not valid
# YAML — Symfony refuses to boot with `Duplicate key "doctrine" detected`. The
# `resolve_target_entities` key goes under the `orm:` that is already in that
# file, beside `mappings`, and it is ONE map: the seam's AreaInterface line and
# this one sit side by side under it.
# WHAT THE FIVE COLUMNS DO WHEN AN ACCOUNT GOES. They go null, and the record
# stays. Removing somebody from the team does not un-walk the patrol they led,
# and a track with no lead is still a track that was walked — the opposite of a
# saved dashboard, which has no meaning once its owner is gone.
# THEN, in this order:
#   bin/console doctrine:migrations:diff      # your history, your migration
#   bin/console doctrine:migrations:migrate
# The bundle ships entities, not migrations: the tables are the bundle's, but
# the migration history is yours, and a vendor replaying its own versions into
# it would fight every `diff` you ever run.
patrol:
resource: '@UhifadhiPatrolBundle/src/Controller/'
type: attribute
